relation_statement: The output readout weights must retain the muP zero initialization so that the model's output scale at init is invariant across model widths when use_mup is enabled.
observable_signal: nonzero L2 norm of the readout weight immediately after initialization; muP coordinate-check activation curves diverging across widths
validity_precondition: use_mup=True and the module is the final output readout (readout-parameterized layer); reset_parameters invoked
evidence_from_issue: ff_out readout reset overwrites muP zero-init weights with normal-distribution values
evidence_from_fix: Fix skips init_normal on ff_out when use_mup is True; non-zero init breaks the muP coordinate-check property and changes the effective output scale

relation_statement: Every transformer block's FFN projection weights must carry the prescribed non-zero normal initialization scale (only the final readout is zero-initialized) when muP is enabled.
observable_signal: per-layer weight std equal to 0 for block FFN projections after init; block FFN output identically zero at the start of training
validity_precondition: use_mup=True; applies to every block's internal FFN projection, not the final readout
evidence_from_issue: OLMoSequentialBlock.ff_proj is silently zero-initialized via MuReadout when use_mup is enabled; wipes out the FFN contribution at start of training
evidence_from_fix: Fix only uses MuReadout for ff_proj when mlp_hidden_size is also set and always re-initializes ff_proj via init_normal

relation_statement: The attention temperature under muP must equal the standard-parameterization value 1/sqrt(d) whenever the head count equals the muP base width, and track muP scaling rules otherwise.
observable_signal: attention logits/outputs differing between muP and SP runs at the base width on identical inputs; scale constant equal to 1/d instead of sqrt(base_heads)/d
validity_precondition: use_mup=True on the scaled-dot-product attention path (not flash varlen)
evidence_from_issue: muP attention scale uses 1/d instead of sqrt(base_d)/d, mismatching the SP scale at the base width
evidence_from_fix: Fix uses sqrt(mup_base_n_heads)/q.size(-1) so the scale matches SP exactly when n_heads == mup_base_n_heads

relation_statement: After a weights-only resume (restore_dataloader=False), all training-progress counters including the global step must be set to the fresh-run value 0 so the LR scheduler replays warmup.
observable_signal: global step nonzero at the first iteration of the new run; initial learning rate far from the expected warmup start value
validity_precondition: resuming from a checkpoint with restore_dataloader=False, i.e. a new run starting from saved weights
evidence_from_issue: global_step not reset when restore_dataloader=False, so resumed runs keep the checkpoint's step counter
evidence_from_fix: restore_checkpoint() resets epoch and token counters but forgot to reset global_step; scheduler starts at e.g. 50000 instead of 0, silently skipping warmup and using a much smaller LR

relation_statement: Metrics all-reduced with SUM across identical model replicas must be divided by the replica count so the logged value equals the true single-replica value.
observable_signal: logged per-param averages and grad-norm metrics exactly num_model_replicas times a single-replica recomputation
validity_precondition: hybrid-sharded data parallelism with num_model_replicas>1 and param-metric collection enabled
evidence_from_issue: Reduced sums/norms not divided by num_model_replicas in HSDP, optimizer metrics inflated by replica count
evidence_from_fix: Fix divides the all-reduced tensors (all_sums_norms_numels and all_norms) by self.num_model_replicas before splitting and using

relation_statement: Weights constructed as muP readout modules must retain the muP-prescribed zero/special initialization so activation magnitudes remain width-invariant when use_mup is enabled.
observable_signal: readout-parameterized weight statistics matching a truncated normal instead of the muP zero init right after reset_parameters; coordinate-check activation magnitudes drifting with width
validity_precondition: use_mup enabled (or an init scheme expecting readout zero-init) and block reset_parameters invoked
evidence_from_issue: Block readout init unconditionally re-initializes ff_proj, overwriting muP zero-init
evidence_from_fix: unconditional init_normal overwrites the MuReadout initialization, silently breaking the muP coordinate-check guarantee that activation magnitudes are width-independent

relation_statement: The constructed q-norm and k-norm modules must both honor the configured elementwise-affine flag so query and key normalization are structurally symmetric under the requested configuration.
observable_signal: learnable affine parameters present in the q-norm while absent in the k-norm when the affine flag is False; parameter count exceeding the configured model
validity_precondition: QK normalization enabled with elementwise affine disabled in the config
evidence_from_issue: q_norm forced to elementwise_affine=True regardless of attention_layer_norm_with_affine
evidence_from_fix: k_norm correctly used elementwise_affine=config.attention_layer_norm_with_affine but q_norm was hard-coded to True, breaking symmetry between q and k and adding parameters the user did not request

relation_statement: The readout weight's initialization statistics must match the configured init scheme delivered through the meta-device materialization path, not the framework default, when init_device is meta.
observable_signal: readout weight std deviating from the configured init std after materialization; readout parameter residing on a real device while all other parameters are on the meta device
validity_precondition: init_device='meta' with sharded-data-parallel lazy materialization expected
evidence_from_issue: ff_out nn.Linear constructed without device=init_device, breaking meta-init flow
evidence_from_fix: omitting the device kwarg meant ff_out was built on the default device with default kaiming init, escaping the init pipeline; the readout carries the wrong init scale

relation_statement: After model materialization, parameter statistics must match the configured init distribution regardless of which parameterization branch (muP with infshapes vs SP baseline) is taken.
observable_signal: parameter statistics stuck at framework-default (often near-zero) values instead of the configured init distribution after loading in the SP branch
validity_precondition: coord-check load_model path used for the standard-parameterization baseline, i.e. infshapes is None
evidence_from_issue: load_model in mup coord-check skips reset_parameters when infshapes is None
evidence_from_fix: reset_parameters() was nested inside `if infshapes is not None:`; the SP baseline skipped it entirely, leaving FSDP-materialized parameters at default values; curves look completely off without raising an error

relation_statement: The learning rate must monotonically decrease after warmup according to the intended warmup-then-decay schedule.
observable_signal: logged learning rate constant at the peak value for every post-warmup step instead of decaying
validity_precondition: trainer configured with a warmup+decay schedule and training long enough that the decay phase matters
evidence_from_issue: DeepSpeed scheduler set to WarmupLR instead of WarmupDecayLR (no decay phase)
evidence_from_fix: WarmupLR only ramps to max LR then holds it constant; the intended WarmupDecayLR ramps then linearly decays; training runs at peak LR for the entire post-warmup duration

relation_statement: The block's residual input must remain unmodified by the attention normalization so the block output equals the input plus the transformed branch (identity path preserved).
observable_signal: checksum of the block input tensor changing across the normalization call (in-place overwrite); block output no longer equal to x + f(norm(x))
validity_precondition: pre-norm residual transformer block with an attention normalization preceding the residual add
evidence_from_issue: Attention norm overwrites residual input — destroys identity path
evidence_from_fix: none provided (root_cause field empty)

relation_statement: Each attention weight's initialization std must scale with that weight's own actual fan-in (in_features**-0.5), not a single model-width constant, under the fan-in-based init method.
observable_signal: empirical post-init weight std of the output projection and K/V projections deviating from in_features**-0.5 when fan-in differs from d_model
validity_precondition: fan-in-scaled init method selected; grouped-query attention (n_kv_heads != n_heads) or output projection whose fan-in differs from d_model
evidence_from_issue: Attention init uses d_model**-0.5 instead of actual w.in_features**-0.5 — wrong std for GQA Q/K/V and w_out
evidence_from_fix: a single std = d_model**-0.5 assumed identical fan-in across all weights; for w_out the actual fan-in is n_heads*head_dim which can differ from d_model; initialization silently scaled wrong

relation_statement: The integer dtype used to read token files must equal the dtype the tokens were stored with whenever the tokenizer vocabulary requires the wider type.
observable_signal: token count per file double the expected length; token-id distribution inconsistent with the source corpus and vocabulary statistics
validity_precondition: tokenizer vocab exceeds 65535 (tokens stored as uint32) and the data source config leaves token_dtype at its default
evidence_from_issue: reads dolma2 (uint32) tokens with default uint16 dtype — silently produces garbage token ids
evidence_from_fix: reading the file as uint16 reinterprets each pair of bytes as a different token, so the model trained on totally fabricated token streams without any error

relation_statement: A configuration must round-trip through encode/decode to an equivalent object, with derived (init=False) fields recomputed on decode rather than restored from a stale snapshot.
observable_signal: decode(encode(cfg)) not equal to cfg — derived field values differing from their post-init recomputation, or constructor failure on unexpected kwargs
validity_precondition: config dataclass declares field(init=False) derived fields and is serialized via as_dict then re-decoded
evidence_from_issue: Config encoding ignores field.init=False — non-init dataclass fields silently round-trip with stale values
evidence_from_fix: as_dict dumped derived fields and re-passed them on decode, which either crashed on unknown kwargs or silently overwrote the post_init-derived value with a stale snapshot, breaking round-trip equivalence

relation_statement: Input activations must be cast to the module's current parameter dtype at call time, not a construction-time snapshot, whenever a wrapper changes parameter dtype after construction.
observable_signal: activation dtype entering the kernel differing from the live conv weight dtype at runtime
validity_precondition: sequence-mixer module wrapped by a sharding wrapper (FSDP/FSDP2) with mixed-precision parameters after construction
evidence_from_issue: Mamba.forward casts inputs using cached self.dtype — wrong dtype after FSDP wraps the conv1d weight
evidence_from_fix: self.dtype was a construction-time snapshot; after FSDP wrapped the inner conv1d the actual parameter dtype changed, so x flowed into the kernel in the wrong precision and produced silently wrong values

relation_statement: The gated-FFN output must include the multiplicative gate branch, i.e. both projections must contribute to the computed output when a SwiGLU FFN is configured.
observable_signal: gate projection weights receiving zero gradient; module output invariant to perturbations of the gate projection weights
validity_precondition: boundary-predictor FFN configured as a standard SwiGLU (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h))
evidence_from_issue: calls F.silu with two arguments — silu treats w3(h) as inplace flag, drops gating
evidence_from_fix: the intended SwiGLU gate (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)) never executed, so the FFN computed silu(w1(h)) alone and the boundary predictor produced silently degraded outputs

relation_statement: During the decay phase the learning-rate multiplier must decrease with training progress following the intended 1-sqrt(1-progress) curve shape.
observable_signal: logged learning rate rising (or with inverted curvature) as progress increases during the decay phase
validity_precondition: sqrt-style decay schedule selected and training within the decay phase
evidence_from_issue: sqrt decay LR schedule uses wrong formula — decay curve inverted
evidence_from_fix: sqrt(progress) instead of 1-sqrt(1-progress) — wrong decay curve shape

relation_statement: Gradient accumulation inside the fused linear+cross-entropy kernel must be performed in fp32 so results match the unfused fp32-accumulation baseline within tolerance under bf16 training.
observable_signal: accumulation dtype bf16 at kernel invocation; loss/gradient trajectories on the LM head diverging from the unfused baseline beyond fp32-accumulation tolerance
validity_precondition: fused linear+CE loss implementation selected under bf16 mixed-precision training
evidence_from_issue: fused_linear_cross_entropy_loss accumulates gradient in bf16 by default — silently noisier than fp32 accumulation
evidence_from_fix: the fused call defaulted accum_grad to bf16, silently degrading gradient precision on the LM head; noise was small enough that training continued but it shifted loss curves vs the unfused baseline

relation_statement: The recorded grad-norm metric must equal the already globally-reduced clipping norm; no additional cross-rank reduction may be applied to it under tensor parallelism.
observable_signal: logged grad-norm differing from the unwrapped full-tensor norm computed at clip time; metric value changing with TP degree while the applied clipping does not
validity_precondition: gradient-clipping callback active with a max-norm configured and TP enabled
evidence_from_issue: Grad clipper recorded grad_norm DTensor — record_metric saw distributed value
evidence_from_fix: with TP clip_grad_norm_ returned a DTensor; the metric system operated on it across ranks, producing a wrongly reduced grad-norm value while clipping itself was already applied locally

relation_statement: The global loss must equal the sum of per-token losses divided by the global count of loss-contributing tokens across the data-parallel group, even when some ranks mask out instances.
observable_signal: loss/gradient magnitude varying with how masked instances are distributed across ranks; per-rank divisor not summing to the global kept-token count
validity_precondition: instance mask present in the batch and at least one rank has masked-out instances; per-rank sum-then-allreduce loss reduction
evidence_from_issue: Instance filter loss divisor missed masked-out instance tokens — wrong gradient scale
evidence_from_fix: ranks with fewer kept tokens contributed an artificially large per-token loss, producing an unfair weighted average across the data-parallel group and a wrong gradient magnitude

relation_statement: Tokens belonging to different documents packed into one sequence must not attend to each other when document-length offsets are provided to the attention backend.
observable_signal: output of a packed sequence differing from per-document unpacked outputs; nonzero attention mass across document boundaries
validity_precondition: attention backend invoked with sequence packing and per-document cumulative lengths supplied
evidence_from_issue: TE attention backend silently ignored cu_doc_lens — intra-doc masking not applied
evidence_from_fix: forward accepted cu_doc_lens / max_doc_len but did not pass them to the kernel; documents packed into a single sequence cross-attended each other — full attention across all packed docs

relation_statement: Attended key positions must be bounded within the configured two-sided window around each query position when sliding-window attention is enabled.
observable_signal: mask admitting key positions beyond one side of the configured window; attention output mismatching a dense reference with the correct two-sided window mask
validity_precondition: flex-attention backend selected with a sliding window configured
evidence_from_issue: sliding-window mask used Python `and` on tensors — short-circuit returned wrong mask
evidence_from_fix: Python's `and` short-circuits on bool() of the first operand, never producing the intended logical AND; the mask was computed as a single one-sided comparison

relation_statement: Parameters designated as frozen (teacher-owned shared blocks) must be excluded from gradient updates during stage-1 distillation training.
observable_signal: checksums/norms of intended-frozen block parameters changing across optimizer steps; nonzero gradients accumulated on the frozen set
validity_precondition: distillation stage-1 with transformer blocks shared between teacher and student and a freeze pattern configured
evidence_from_issue: BLT stage1 froze only teacher.* — student blocks updated against teacher gradient
evidence_from_fix: because blocks are shared, the actual block parameters live under 'blocks.*' and were not matched by the freeze pattern, so they were unfrozen and trained against gradients including the teacher path

relation_statement: Each distillation loss component must be divided by its own position count (byte positions for the byte loss, patch positions for the patch loss) so the components are weighted as configured.
observable_signal: ratio of byte-loss to patch-loss contributions deviating from the configured weighting; divisor equal to the raw input element count instead of the component's position count
validity_precondition: distillation transformer with a patch-loss division factor configured
evidence_from_issue: BLTDistill patch loss div factor used input_ids.numel() — wrong scaling for byte-level losses
evidence_from_fix: the correct denominator is the number of byte positions, with an analogous division by patch positions for the patch loss; the mismatch silently mis-weighted byte vs patch loss components

relation_statement: Dataset instances served from an on-disk cache must structurally match the active configuration, which requires the cache fingerprint to include every layout-determining field (sequence length, BOS token, max target length).
observable_signal: returned instance layout/length not matching the configured sequence length; cache hit despite a changed layout-determining setting
validity_precondition: fixed-sequence-length dataset variants with cached offsets/packed indices reused across runs whose sequence settings changed
evidence_from_issue: FSLDataset fingerprint missed sequence_length / bos_token_id — wrong cache reused
evidence_from_fix: cached instance offsets computed under previous values were reused when those settings changed, so the dataset returned instances whose actual layout no longer matched the configured sequence_length

relation_statement: The loss tensor passed to backward must remain attached to the computation graph so that every configured loss component contributes gradient for all values of the mixing coefficient.
observable_signal: gradient norm collapsing to ~0 while the reported loss stays finite as the soft-loss weight decays; combined-loss components lacking grad_fn
validity_precondition: soft-CE distillation branch active while the head returns its CE and z-loss terms as detached copies
evidence_from_issue: soft_ce branch backprops only alpha*soft_ce — hard_ce gradient zeroed because output.ce_loss is detached
evidence_from_fix: combined_loss was built from .detach()'d ce_loss/z_loss; only output.loss carries gradient, so once alpha decayed to 0 backward() saw zero gradient and grad_norm collapsed
